description: This collection welcomes original pre-clinical and clinical studies on CNS injuries, focusing on diverse aspects in pathophysiology, diagnosis, treatment and rehabilitation strategies.

title: Emergent phases in materials under nonequilibrium excitation
description: In this cross-journal Collection, we highlight articles that identify and characterize emergent phases and their mechanisms under nonequilibrium excitation conditions.

title: Initially Anode-less and Anode-free Batteries
description: This cross-journal Collection highlights cutting-edge research that investigates critical topics such as current collector design, interfacial chemistry, and electrolyte engineering to address the challenges associated with the demanding conditions in initially anode-less (N/P < 1) and anode-free (N/P = 0) batteries.

title: High-resolution modeling for Earth system
description: In this cross-journal collection, we showcase articles that highlight advances enabled by high-resolution simulations as well as advances in high-resolution model development.

title: Medical Ultrasound: Emerging Techniques and Applications
description: This cross-journal Collection showcases the broad and exciting field of emerging techniques and applications in medical ultrasound.

title: Functional Soil Ecology
description: We welcome contributions across a broad range of topics, including microbial and faunal functional traits, biogeochemical processes, soil–plant interactions, ecosystem services, methodological developments, and applications that support sustainable land management.

title: Peptide drug design
description: We are interested in methodological studies, including both computational and experimental approaches for designing new peptide therapeutics. We also welcome research presenting experimentally validated design of novel peptides.

title: Coral Biology Under Climate Stress
description: Editors invite manuscripts that advance the scientific understanding of coral stress responses and climate resilience across molecular, physiological, ecological, and restoration focused dimensions.

title: Microfluidic advances in biosensing, biofabrication, and next generation microreactors
description: This Collection aims to highlight the expanding capabilities of microfluidics in probing, manipulating, and engineering biological systems across scales.

title: The expanding therapeutic landscape of GLP 1 receptor agonists
description: This Collection calls for papers that investigate the expanding clinical and biological roles of GLP‑1 RAs. We welcome studies that examine the mechanisms underlying their metabolic and weight‑loss effects, along with clinical research evaluating their use in cardiovascular and cardiometabolic disease, hepatic disorders, and neurological conditions, including neurodegenerative processes.

title: Catalyst design for C1 chemistry
description: This Collection showcases how mechanistic understanding of active sites, reaction pathways, and deactivation can be translated into rational catalyst design to improve selectivity, stability, and process efficiency in heterogeneous thermocatalysis.

title: Neurodegeneration and the role of immunopathology
description: In this cross-journal Collection, the editors at Nature Neuroscience, Nature Immunology, Nature Communications and Communications Medicine aim to bring together cutting-edge research exploring the mechanistic and diagnostic intersections between immune dysregulation and neuronal decline.

title: Structural biology of viral nano machines
description: This collection highlights research on viral nanomachines used by bacterial and animal viruses to recognize hosts, replicate, and assemble infectious particles.

title: Neuromorphic Vision Systems
description: This collection aims to bring together cutting-edge research of neuromorphic vision hardware and algorithms, spanning from hardware-software codesigns to real-world deployments.

title: Generative Models in Engineering Biology
description: This cross-journal Collection aims to bring together the latest and most compelling demonstration of generative models used for engineering biology, covering a range of fields where the resulting achievement is an engineered biological system.

title: Implementation Science in Public Health
description: With this cross-journal collection, the editors of Nature Communications, Nature Health, and Communications Health invite submissions that advance understanding of implementation research as a comprehensive approach to investigating and improving the effectiveness of interventions in real world settings.

title: Sustainable strategies for low carbon cement, concrete, and steel
description: We invite contributions that improve material efficiency, introduce new material technologies, lowers carbon emissions and support sustainable construction pathways.

title: Bridging environmental microbes to human, animal and planetary health
description: With this cross-journal Collection, the editors at Nature Communications, and Communications Health invite manuscripts that highlight research efforts to connect data on environmental microbial surveillance, detection and epidemiology with human, animal and planetary health, as well as sustainability goals.

title: Electric Vehicle Battery Repurposing, Recycling and Regenerating
description: This collection brings together research that tackles the remaining technical challenges, which include capacity/power estimation at the pack, fault diagnosis, sorting, consistency evaluation, safety, and efficient and effective material recovery, regeneration and upcycling.

title: Quantum machine learning: understanding capabilities, limitations, and perspectives for quantum advantage
description: This Collection highlights articles that investigate the capabilities and limitations of QML models, aiming at clarifying the prospects for quantum advantage in the near future.

title: Active, Entangled or Confined: Polymer Physics Across Synthetic and Living Matter
description: This Collection aims to unite research from diverse disciplines, encompassing theoretical, computational, and experimental studies that elucidate links between geometry, molecular architecture, and dynamical observables.

title: Microphysiological systems for advanced modeling, high-throughput evaluation, and clinical translation
description: This cross-journal Collection highlights engineering advances, promote high-throughput evaluation for translational applications, or enhance biological and clinical relevance of next-generation Microphysiological Systems, such as 3D culture systems, organs-on-chips, and microfluidic platforms.

title: Complex Trait Genetics: From Association to Function
description: With this cross-journal Collection, the editors at Nature Communications, Communications Biology and Scientific Reports invite manuscripts that move beyond locus discovery to provide functional and mechanistic insights into genetic associations, including through fine-mapping, multi-omics integration, single-cell or spatial approaches, and in vitro/in vivo studies.

title: Models in Cancer Research
description: With this cross-journal Collection, the editors at Nature Cancer, Nature Communications, Communications Biology and Scientific Reports invite original research Articles that focus on the use of existing or the establishment of novel experimental cancer models to shed light on all aspects of tumour biology.

title: Visual Imagery
description: Editors invite manuscripts that highlight recent developments in the mechanisms, functions and experience of visual mental imagery. Topics include, but are not limited to, neural mechanisms of visual imagery, aphantasia, hyperphantasia, methods of assessing visual imagery, and cognitive processes related to visual imagery.

title: Mitochondrial Quality Control
description: This Collection aims to unite diverse research spanning mitochondrial dynamics, cristae morphology, membrane regulation, lipid and protein–lipid composition, surveillance pathways, and the cellular responses that restore or eliminate damaged mitochondria.

title: Interpretable models for spatial transcriptomics
description: With this collection, the editors invite manuscripts presenting interpretable models for analysis of spatial transcriptomic data.

title: Biohybrid Robotics
description: This Collection welcomes studies that advance biohybrid robots as functional machines.

title: Neurobiology and neural circuits of parenting behaviours
description: With this collection, the editors at Nature Communications, Communications Biology and Scientific Reports welcome the submission of primary research articles that focus on neuronal circuits and behaviour involved in both male and female parenting behaviors. We particularly encourage studies in rodent models exploring the intersection of parenting behavior, motivation and epigenetics with an emphasis on neurobiology probed using methods such as transcriptomics, optogenetics, chemogenetics and in vivo recording.

title: Organotropism in cancer metastasis
description: This collection aims to highlight recent advances in the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying the complexity of metastatic organotropism, and how these actionable insights could be leveraged to facilitate early detection and diagnosis of metastasis, as well as the development of targeted therapeutic approaches.

title: Earthquake forecasting and early warning
description: This cross-journal collection highlights recent progress in understanding earthquake processes, as well as current challenges and future pathways towards more reliable forecasting and effective early warning systems.

title: Mechanisms of Tissue Fibrosis
description: Editors welcome original Articles exploring the cellular and molecular mechanisms of fibrosis, such as fibroblast activation, fibrogenic signalling pathways, immune–stromal interactions, and extracellular matrix remodelling.

title: Organoid models for infectious diseases
description: Editors welcome the submission of primary research Articles focusing on recent advances of stem cell-based organoid models for studying infectious diseases, and novel insights in the disease mechanisms of human infections with the support of stem cell-based organoid systems.

title: The Lunar South
description: With this cross-journal Collection, the editors highlight articles that advance our understanding of the geology and surface features of the southern regions of the Moon.

title: Ultra processed food and health

title: Microbiome and energy metabolism
description: This collection invites research on microbial energy metabolism including studies characterizing microbial metabolic pathways or impacts of microbial metabolites on host metabolism.

title: The Gut-Brain axis and health
description: This Collection seeks to unite research on the interplay between metabolic and neurological functions, focusing on topics such as the role of the gut microbiome in modulating mental health and metabolic disorders, the influence of nutritional status and diet on the gut-brain axis, the impact of therapeutic interventions such as GLP-1 agonists, mechanisms linking gut health and mental well-being, the role of gut hormones in metabolic regulation, and inter-organ communication in health and disease.

title: Solvation structure engineering in battery electrolytes for demanding operating conditions
description: This cross-journal Collection highlights cutting‑edge research on electrolyte solvation structure engineering that advances molecular design, interfacial chemistry, and electrolyte formulations to enable high-voltage cycling, fast-charging and high-power capabilities and/or wide-temperature range operation.

title: Implantable wireless communication technologies
description: This collection brings together research that addresses critical engineering challenges in implantable wireless communications. It demonstrates how electromagnetic, optical, acoustic, or hybrid methods can be engineered to achieve reliable wireless communications and power delivery through biological tissues.

title: Adolescent mental health: advancing understanding to improve outcomes
description: This cross-journal collection invites manuscripts that investigate the distribution and determinants of adolescent mental health across diverse settings as well as innovative prevention, detection and intervention approaches.

title: Viral infections and the nervous system
description: This collection invites research on the neuropathogenesis of viral infections at the molecular, cellular, tissues, host and population level.

title: PFAS and forever chemicals in the environment
description: With this cross-journal Collection, the editors invite manuscripts that highlight recent advances in understanding the fate, transport, and effects of persistent pollutants on human health and ecosystems.

title: Plastids: from Phylogeny to Physiology
description: With this cross-journal Collection, the editors at Communications Biology, Nature Communications, Nature Plants, and Scientific Reports invite manuscripts from diverse perspectives that investigate plastid biology or explore the fundamental principles governing plastid origin, integration, and diversification across the eukaryotic tree of life.

title: Brain and body physiology in changing ecosystems
description: This cross-journal Collection welcomes submissions that highlight mechanisms underlying neural and physiological responses to contemporary environmental changes.

title: Confined Plasmas and Nuclear Fusion
description: This cross-journal collection aims at exploring a wide range of topics in confined plasmas and nuclear fusion research and invites original research contributions from a variety of devices and laboratories.

title: Digital Medicine for Infectious Diseases

description: This cross-journal Collection focuses on approaches that use nonlinear dynamical systems to uncover organizing principles in living systems, together with experiments that are explicitly interpreted through such frameworks.

title: Structural biology of biomolecular condensation
description: This Collection invites work on the structural biology of the interactions, regulation, and disease-associated disruptions of biomolecular condensates.

With this cross-journal Collection, the editors at Nature Communications, Communications Biology and Scientific Reports invite manuscripts that highlight advances in our understanding of the mechanisms underlying transposition and its regulation, as well as manuscripts that shed light into how transposons affect genome structure and their roles in health and disease. Only original research Articles will be considered for this collection.

title: Crosstalk Between Tissue-Resident Adaptive and Innate Memory Cells

title: Hazards in Mountain Regions

title: Self-healing chemical systems

title: Tumor Microenvironment Crosstalk and Therapeutic Implications
description: With this cross-journal Collection, the editors at Nature Immunology, Nature Communications, Communications Medicine and Scientific Reports invite manuscripts that highlight cutting-edge research on TME crosstalk and its therapeutic implications. Topics of interest include immune modulation and checkpoint pathways, cancer-associated fibroblasts and stromal remodeling, angiogenesis and vascular normalization, metabolic reprogramming within the TME, and the role of microbiota in tumor-immune dynamics. We also welcome studies on novel therapeutic approaches that exploit TME vulnerabilities to advance cancer treatment.

title: Managing landscapes after land abandonment: afforestation, rewilding and restoration
description: This collection invites insights on managing post-abandonment landscapes—afforest, rewild, restore—balancing biodiversity, climate resilience, and equity.

title: Plant Epigenetics and Epigenomics
description: With this cross-journal Collection, the editors at Nature Communications, Communications Biology and Scientific Reports invite manuscripts that highlight how epigenetics shapes plant development, stress responses and adaptation. We also welcome studies developing and utilizing advanced technologies such as epigenomic mapping, single cell epigenomics, and multi-omics approaches to provide insights into plant epigenetic mechanisms.

title: Total Synthesis and Chemistry of Natural Products
description: This cross-journal Collection highlights manuscripts on total synthesis, including innovative methodology, retrosynthetic design, bioinspired strategies, AI-assisted retrosynthesis, and emerging technologies such as automation and high-throughput experimentation; as well as natural product discovery and diversification.

title: Cell death and inflammatory signalling

We also encourage contributions that develop or evaluate best practices for the design, conduct, and reporting of One Health research, as well as studies that address barriers and opportunities for translating One Health principles into policy and practice.

title: Critical materials supply chain sustainability
description: With this cross-journal Collection, the editors invite manuscripts that offer novel insights into resilient supply chains, digital transformation, circularity in materials, and governance for a secure energy transition.

title: Light Signaling in Plants
description: This collection will highlight studies that uncover the mechanisms of light signal transduction and harness these discoveries to address challenges in food security and climate change.

title: Plant Membrane Biology
description: Editors highlight plant membranes—their remarkable ability to remodel, package proteins and mediate trafficking; their chemical composition; and their protein constituents that include transporters and channels that facilitate molecular exchange, receptors and ligands that initiate signalling, and enzymes whose reactions power the cell, sort proteins, regulate pH and scavenge.

description: This cross-journal collection will consider submissions of research articles that highlight advances in nanomedicine aimed at overcoming cancer treatment failure, as well as nanotechnology used to uncover the underlying biological mechanisms of such failure.

description: This collection highlights innovative approaches that reduce complexity and cost in the design, fabrication, and deployment of optical imaging technologies.

title: Infectious disease modelling for health policy
description: With this cross-journal collection, Communications Health, and Nature Communications invite Articles describing the application of infectious disease models to timely health policy questions.

title: Immune mechanisms in arthritis
description: This cross-journal collection welcomes original research articles spanning basic, translational, and clinical studies that explore the immune mechanisms influencing arthritis pathogenesis.

description: With this cross-journal Collection, the editors at Nature Immunology, Nature Communications, Communications Biology and Scientific Reports invite original research Articles investigating all aspects of the complex molecular interplay between pathogens and their human and/or animal hosts.

title: Muscle biology
description: In this collection, the editors of Nature Metabolism, Communications Biology, Nature Communications, and Scientific Reports aim to highlight cutting-edge research in muscle biology.

title: Orbitronics and unconventional spin-orbit torque for next-generation magnetic memory and spin logic devices
description: This Collection highlights progress in the manipulation of magnetic states through spin-orbit interactions and orbital phenomena for robust, versatile, energy-efficient memory and logic devices.

title: Physical Activity and Mental Health
description: This Collection features research on the intersection of physical activity and mental health, exploring whether and how activity can influence mental well-being positively or otherwise.

title: Methods development in Cryo-ET and in situ structural determination
description: The editors invite manuscripts that highlight methodological developments in instrument design, sample preparation, data acquisition, data analysis, interpretation and integration from different techniques.

title: Diagnosis and Care of Sepsis
description: With this cross-journal Collection, the editors at Communications Medicine, Nature Communications, and Scientific Reports invite manuscripts that highlight diagnostic techniques and treatment modalities for confronting sepsis.

title: Sustainable agricultural practices
description: In this cross-journal collection we focus on current research to optimize resource use and enhance ecosystem services.

title: Deep-Sea Mining
description: This cross-journal collection presents articles that advance our knowledge of deep-sea mining, in terms of impacts and management.

title: Neurocognitive perspectives on language comprehension
description: The Editors at Communications Psychology, Nature Communications, and Scientific Reports invite submissions providing neurocognitive perspectives on language comprehension.

title: Climate adaptation and resilience in urban and rural communities
description: In this cross-journal collection, we showcase studies that focus on adaptation in urban and rural areas.

title: Immune cell engineering for cancer therapy 2026
description: With this Collection, a partnership between Nature Communications, Communications Medicine, Communications Biology, and Scientific Reports, we welcome submissions of primary research papers that focus on immune cell engineering for cancer therapy. The journals are particularly interested in preclinical studies proposing new engineering strategies and therapeutic developments.

title: Life Course Epidemiology
description: This Collection explores how biological, environmental, and social factors across the lifespan shape health outcomes, with particular attention to chronic disease, multimorbidity, and healthy aging. title: Healthy Islands
description: This cross-journal collection invites submissions of papers that advance our understanding of all aspects of health in the Pacific Islands.

description: This cross-journal collection highlights a wide range of research spanning geopolitical and territorial claims, cultural heritage and Indigenous communities, and food and water security, among others.

description: This cross-journal Collection invites manuscripts that highlight advances in the fundamentals and applications of multinuclear complexes and small inorganic clusters.

title: Biosensing
description: With this cross-journal Collection, the editors of Communications Biology, Nature Biomedical Engineering, Nature Sensors, Nature Communications, and Scientific Reports welcome the submission of primary research Articles focusing on the development of engineered biosensing devices with the potential to be applied in biomedical research and in the management of disease conditions.

description: This cross-journal Collection between Communications Physics, Nature Communications and Scientific Reports brings together the advances in Crystal polymorphism in Soft and Functional Materials.

title: Cortical-subcortical brain loops

title: Ecological Consequences of Nano- and Microplastics
description: This cross-journal Collection invites research that investigates the ecological impacts of nano- and microplastics.

title: RNA biology in plant biotic interactions
description: The editors invite articles in all areas of research investigating the roles of RNA in plant biotic interactions.

title: Proteolysis in Plants
description: The objective of this collection is to provide a comprehensive overview of the latest research on the molecular mechanisms, regulatory networks and roles of proteolysis in plants under both physiological and stress conditions.

title: Sustainable waste management through polymer upcycling
description: This Collection invites innovative research that transforms waste into new materials or products in smart, energy efficient, scalable and eco-friendly ways through polymer upcycling.

title: Gender equity in academia and research
description: This Collection invites research examining the intersection of gender identity and the academic research environment.

title: Lifespan changes in the human brain
description: This cross-journal collection invites submissions that investigate human brain changes across all or multiple stages of life, from in-utero to older age.

title: Neuroengineering
description: With this cross-journal Collection, the editors at Nature Biomedical Engineering, Nature Medicine, Nature Neuroscience, Nature Biotechnology, Nature Communications, Communications Medicine, Communications Biology, and Scientific Reports invite manuscripts that highlight the development, use and insight obtained from applying neuroengineering approaches.

title: Sensing Technologies for Crop Health and Growth
description: With this cross-journal Collection, we invite manuscripts that highlight continual or real-time sensing systems of any form, primarily for arable farming or crop production.

title: Comparative Psychology of Cognition, Affect, and Behaviour
description: With this cross-journal Collection, the editors at Communications Psychology, Nature Communications and Scientific Reports invite manuscripts that highlight recent progress in Comparative Psychology.

title: Synthetic Catalysts for Biomedicine and Biotechnology
description: In this cross-journal Collection between Nature Communications, Nature Chemical Biology, Communications Chemistry, Communications Materials, Communications Sustainability and Scientific Reports, we aim to bring together the latest advances in synthetic catalysts for biomedicine and biotechnology, covering design and production, mechanistic studies, and application demonstrations.

title: Towards low-pressure all-solid-state batteries
description: This Cross-journal Collection highlights advances in the development of low- or zero-pressure all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs).

title: High-Energy Light Sources - From Tabletop to Large Facilities
description: This cross-journal collection born in collaboration between Communications Physics, Nature Communications and Scientific Reports explores recent progress in high-energy light sources, from from tabletop to large scale facilities.

title: NeuroAI and Embodied Intelligence
description: This cross-journal Collection brings together research at the intersection of neuroscience, artificial intelligence, neuromorphic hardware, and robotics with a focus on how insights from brain function can inspire the design of more adaptive, efficient, and intelligent systems. We welcome submissions that explore neurobiologically-inspired models, architectures, and learning algorithms that have the potential to enhance embodied AI and robotic systems.

title: Generative AI for mechanical engineering design and optimization
description: In this collection we aim to publish exciting advances in the capability of generative AI methods and their application directions within a broad mechanical engineering scope.

title: Understanding species redistributions under global climate change
description: With this cross-journal Collection, we invite submissions of articles that use modern approaches to advance the understanding in species redistributions under global climate change.

title: Healthy Aging
description: This collection welcomes submissions based on studying preclinical models, as well as population-wide and clinical studies. Studies that advance our understanding of mechanisms behind healthy aging are also welcomed. Clinical research of interest will include epidemiological studies, observational studies, longitudinal cohort studies, systematic reviews and clinical trials.

title: (In)civility
description: With this cross-journal Collection, the editors at Communications Psychology, Nature Communications, and Scientific Reports invite innovative research on incivility.

title: Global Cancer Care: Obstacles, Solutions, and Impact on Survivorship
description: This cross-journal collection welcomes submissions of research Articles and Registered Reports that highlight developments in understanding barriers to cancer care and strategies to improve them in different regions.

title: Mechanisms and impact of 3D genome organisation
description: This collection welcomes submissions investigating mechanisms of TAD formation and maintenance, chromatin looping and gene regulation, impact of 3D genome on transcriptional landscapes and high-throughput methods for studying genome organisation.

title: Artificial Intelligence Methodology in Structural Biology
description: In this joint collection between Communications Biology, Nature Communications, Nature Structural & Molecular Biology, and Scientific Reports, we invite submissions containing new methods for the prediction of structure of macromolecules such as proteins, peptides and RNA.

title: CMOS-compatible semiconductor qubits
description: With this cross-journal Collection, the editors at Nature Communications, Communications Physics and Scientific Reports invite manuscripts that advance the fundamental physics of CMOS-compatible semiconductor qubits, tackle scalability issues, and showcase practical applications in quantum computing, communication, and simulation.

title: Signalling Pathways of Innate Immunity
description: In this cross-journal Collection, we invite research into the complex signalling pathways of innate immunity, emphasising the activation and regulation of pattern recognition receptors in response to microbial and endogenous triggers.

title: Targeted diagnostics and therapies for autoimmune diseases
description: This cross-journal Collection welcomes pre-clinical, translational, clinical and public health research addressing the complexities of immune-mediated diseases and their management.

title: Artificial intelligence in RNA biology
description: With this cross-journal Collection, the editors at Nature Communications and Communications Biology invite manuscripts that showcase the development and application of AI-driven approaches leveraging big data to advance our understanding of RNA biology.

title: DNA repair and human disease
description: This cross-journal Collection between Nature Communications, Communications Biology and Scientific Reports welcomes submissions on the mechanisms of DNA repair using multiple modelling systems and the applications of DNA repair mechanisms in human disease diagnosis and treatment.

title: Health outcomes of adversity in early life
description: This cross-journal collection welcomes submissions investigating any health outcome resulting from adversity experienced in early life, including studies focused on prevention, epidemiological factors, pathophysiological mechanisms, the impact of socioeconomic factors, or advances in treatment options.

title: Adolescent and adult autism
description: The Editors at Communications Psychology and Nature Communications invite research on autism in adolescence or adulthood.

title: Reward and anti-reward circuits in health and disease
description: This cross-journal Collection welcomes submissions on novel reward and anti-reward mechanisms regulating motivated behaviors in health and disease.

title: Registered Reports
description: Registered Reports are an article format aimed at promoting robust and rigorous scientific practices. This collection features our published Registered Reports, as well as relevant editorials and other related content.

title: Replication and generalization
description: This Collection invites submissions of direct replication and generalization studies of primary research papers in psychology.

title: Emotions in politics: democratic participation, belonging and division
description: This Collection aims to advance interdisciplinary research on the role of emotions in political participation, democratic life and collective political identities.

title: Far-right mobilisation and democratic transformation
description: This Humanities and Social Sciences Communications Collection examines the contemporary dynamics of far-right mobilisation and its implications for democracy. We invite interdisciplinary contributions from political science, sociology, media studies, history, law, anthropology, and related fields that explore how far-right actors mobilise, gain legitimacy, interact with institutions and opponents, and influence democratic life across different context

title: Political trust: trends, crises, and measurement
description: This Collection invites scholarship that examines political trust as a dynamic, multidimensional phenomenon.

title: Pharmaceutical intellectual property
description: This Collection invites submissions addressing the multifaceted legal, economic, ethical, and policy dimensions of pharmaceutical intellectual property from diverse disciplinary perspectives and geographical contexts.

title: Beyond the classroom: alternative education across contexts
description: This Collection examines alternative forms of education and their social, cultural, political, and psychological implications. We invite research that explores alternative educational practices, including community-led learning, informal and non-formal education, experimental pedagogies, digital learning spaces, and decolonial or indigenous knowledge systems.

title: Crisis and resilience in Latin American politics
description: This Collection seeks to explore continuity and change in Latin American politics in both historical and contemporary perspectives.

title: Museums and archives as educational institutions
description: This Collection invites interdisciplinary scholarship that examines museums and archives as sites of formal and informal education, exploring their pedagogical strategies, social responsibilities, and transformative potential.

title: Nationalism and national identity in contemporary politics and society
description: The aim of this Humanities and Social Sciences Communications Collection is to bring together interdisciplinary perspectives on nationalism and national identity to critically examine their roles in contemporary politics, society, and culture.

title: Contemporary dialogues in global critical theory
description: This Collection aims to explore social, political, and academic debates that have emerged specifically in the 21st Century and are crucial for the development of our global societies.

title: Grievances and victimhood in social and political engagement
description: This Collection explores how grievance and victimhood shape political and social engagement, particularly the social and behavioural psychological dimensions of grievance formation, mobilisation, and political expression.

title: Food politics in the Global South
description: This Humanities and Social Sciences Communications Collection seeks critical, interdisciplinary reflections on the politics of food in the Global South. We welcome empirical and theoretical contributions from political science, sociology, anthropology, economics, history, development studies, environmental studies, and related fields.

title: Translating across cultures: literature, film and other media
description: This Collection invites interdisciplinary scholarship that explores translation as a cultural, aesthetic, and political practice across literature, film, and other media.

title: Sign Languages: acquisition, application and transmission
description: This Collection seeks to explore sign languages as linguistic, cultural, and social phenomena.

title: The politics of museums and national monuments
description: This Collection invites interdisciplinary scholarship that interrogates the politics of museums and national monuments.

title: Forced displacement and migration
description: This Collection invites interdisciplinary research that explores the causes, consequences, and responses to forced displacement.

title: Art and design in the age of AI
description: This Collection invites scholarship that explores the intersections of art, design, and artificial intelligence from across the humanities and social sciences.

title: Zombies in culture, society, and thought
description: This Collection invites interdisciplinary scholarship that engages with the zombie as a cultural, philosophical, and social figure.

title: Environmental advocacy: psychological and behavioural dynamics
description: This Collection explores the psychological and behavioural dynamics of environmental activism, with a view to understanding how people engage with climate issues - from everyday behaviour to large-scale protest movements.

title: Burnout
description: This Collection invites scholarship that explores burnout from across the humanities and social sciences.

title: Fiscal policies and energy vulnerability: tackling fuel and energy poverty in a changing global landscape
description: This Collection seeks to address the urgent and evolving intersection of fiscal policy and energy poverty, a critical issue amid recent international crises, climate transition imperatives, and rising energy costs.

title: Hinduism – belief, politics and culture
description: This Collection looks to explore Hinduism and its place in the world today, welcoming research on the everyday lives of modern Hindus, the religion's links to politics, and also the cultural imprint of Hinduism on society.

title: All loved up – exploring love in everyday life
description: This Collection is interested in scholarship that examines love in all its everyday expressions. How is love expressed across different cultures, identities and social positions?

title: Trauma: social and psychological dimensions
description: This Collection invites contributions that explore trauma as a socially embedded, psychologically complex and politically situated phenomenon, with particular attention to its transcultural, transethnic and transgenerational dimensions.

title: Nuclear contamination in the Arctic
description: This Collection explores the intersections of nuclear risk, environmental safety policy, and geopolitical contestation in the Arctic. It investigates how contamination is managed, and how affected communities navigate long-term consequences.

title: Research futures: opportunities, challenges, and competitiveness of doctoral and early-career researchers
description: This Collection aims to generate a comprehensive, interdisciplinary exploration of the evolving conditions of doctoral and early-career research, including both challenges and opportunities.

title: Reflections of the body: media, culture and image perception
description: This Collection explores the intersections of body image with cultural norms, power structures and digital media, including within underrepresented or marginalised communities.

title: Arctic exceptionalism amidst emerging global tensions
description: This Collection explores the increasing pressure on the cooperative and peaceful shared governance of the Arctic, due to rising global geopolitical tension.

title: Transdisciplinary research for transformative change: from conceptual insights to societal impact
description: This article Collection aims to advance transdisciplinary and transformative conceptual and methodological approaches to societal and global challenges.

title: Cultures of command: identity, power, and belonging in global militaries
description: This collection explores the cultural dimensions of military life across global contexts, with an interest in how armed forces construct and challenge ideas of gender, race, nationalism, professionalism, and sacrifice.

title: Political participation and mobilisation in Central and Eastern Europe
description: This Collection aims to facilitate interdisciplinary dialogue on political participation and mobilisation in Central and Eastern Europe by examining historical trajectories, contemporary practices, and emerging trends.

title: Buddhism - beliefs, politics and culture
description: This Collection explores Buddhism and its place in the world today. The Collection is interested in the belief, culture and politics of this major religion, welcoming research on the everyday lives of modern Buddhists, the religion's links to politics, and also the cultural imprint of Buddhism on society.

title: Innovation, AI, and education
description: This Collection seeks to explore the multifaceted intersections between innovation, artificial intelligence, and education.

title: Psychology of racism and prejudice
description: This Collection investigates the psychology of racism and prejudice, bringing together insights from cognitive, social, developmental, and cultural psychology, as well as sociology, history, and anthropology.

title: The economics of social mobility
description: This Collection invites research that explores social mobility primarily from the perspective of economics, including labour economics, public finance, development economics, and macroeconomics.

title: Human-animal interactions and relations
description: Humans’ inter-relation with non-human animals is a ubiquitous feature of contemporary life, whether through the clothes we wear, the food we eat, how we decide what are invaders or pests, and the company we keep. This Humanities and Social Sciences Collection invites scholarship (empirical, theoretical, qualitative and quantitative) that sheds light on these relationships in different contexts and settings and from a wide array of disciplinary vantage points, including cultural studies, sociology, anthropology, psychology, history, philosophy, economics, literature, gender studies, indigenous studies and environmental humanities. Research that is not primarily rooted in the humanities and social sciences will not be considered. Clinical or physiological studies are not in scope.

title: In search of happiness: rethinking well-being and the good life
description: This Collection is interested in research that explores what contributes to happiness, how it is experienced and measured, and what can be done to promote it at both individual and societal levels.

title: Contemporary Catholicism(s): global perspectives on belief, power and identity
description: This Collection seeks to critically examine the political, social and cultural dimensions of Catholicism today, including interdisciplinary perspectives, that explore Catholicism.

title: The anatomy of hate and violence
description: This Collection aims to explore the origins, mechanisms and consequences of hate and violence, from incel culture and online radicalisation to democratic breakdowns and policy implications.

title: Critical simulation studies
description: This Humanities and Social Sciences Communications Collection invites scholars to explore the empirical growth of simulation across a wide range of domains. There will be a cross-cutting emphasis on the digital aspects of simulation, including algorithms, large language models (GenAI), bots, and technology platforms.

title: Emotion regulation
description: This Humanities and Social Sciences Communications Collection aims to explore the multi-layered dynamics of emotion regulation, assessing the impacts of both individual and social processes on its mechanisms, contexts, functions and consequences.

title: Decolonising economics: justice, plurality, and inclusivity
description: This Collection invites contributions that engage with the theme of decolonising economics, both theoretically and practically, exploring its implications for economic thought and transformative action.

title: Cultural perspectives in emotions research
description: This Humanities and Social Sciences Communications Collection explores the role of cultural perspectives within emotional research, and aims to advance knowledge of how emotions are experienced, interpreted and expressed across different cultures.

title: Natural disaster preparation and policy
description: This Collection examines how societies anticipate, prepare for, and respond to disasters, and how governmental policies shape - and are shaped by - existing or outdated strategies, new threats, and health, gender or racial inequalities.

title: Reframing artificial intelligence: critical perspectives from AI social science
description: To untangle the links between technological and social forces, this Collection invites social science perspectives to advance the study of AI’s sociotechnical, cultural and political dimensions.

title: Rethinking the blue economy: sustainability, equity and ocean futures
description: This Collection seeks contributions that critically engage with the blue economy as both a policy agenda and a field of practice, exploring its implications across political, ecological and economic domains.

title: Terrorism, radicalisation and social order: perspectives on emerging threats and responses
description: This Humanities and Social Sciences Communications Collection invites research papers examining terrorism and terrorist threats through the lenses of political science, sociology and related disciplines. We welcome original research that explores the causes, dynamics and consequences of terrorism, as well as responses to it, in both contemporary and historical contexts.

title: Loneliness and social isolation
description: This Collection invites research that sheds light on loneliness, social isolation and related themes, such as what makes people lonely or socially isolated, and what can be done to alleviate negative effects

title: Large language models in psychological science
description: This Collection specifically aims to explore the value and impact of LLMs in psychological measurement, experimentation, and practice.

title: Education in the Anthropocene
description: This Collection explores learning and pedagogy as a backdrop to navigate the barriers of the renewed aspiration of a transition economy.

title: From bits of history to bytes of data: AI and the study of the ancient Near East
description: This Collection aims at examining the computational and digital study of “greater Western Asia” and its epistemological implications.

title: Tourists, go home? Sustainable tourism in popular destinations
description: This Collection is dedicated to addressing complex problems arising from tourism in high-demand destinations.

title: Isobenefit urbanism
description: This Collection explores the concept of Isobenefit urbanism; a design idea focused on high quality, localised and walkable cities.

title: Culture in code: intercultural competence in the age of AI and globalisation
description: This Collection explores complex interactions between cutting-edge technological advancements and the intricate tapestry of cultural interactions.

title: Divisive politics, polarisation and democratic decline
description: This collection sets out to take a holistic view of what has been termed ‘nasty politics’ and its implications for society and democracy.

title: Philosophy [in:of:for:and] digital knowledge infrastructures
description: This Collection will bring together philosophical contributions concerning digital knowledge infrastructure, broadly construed.

title: Toponymy and toponomastics at the intersection between language contact and historical geography
description: This Collection welcomes research on themes related to toponymy and toponomastics at the intersection between language and historical geography.

title: Expertise in integration and implementation for transformative research
description: Collection examining the specialised knowledge, skills, competencies and dispositional attributes required to identify which disciplinary and stakeholder knowledges are relevant, synthesise different perspectives, manage power imbalances and legacies of colonisation in researching problems, and accommodate conflicting values and world views, including across different cultures.

title: Humanising epidemiology: non-medical investigations into epi/pandemic phenomena
description: This Collection welcomes research that examines the role and contributions of the social sciences in shaping the global response to public health crises.

title: Continuity and change in Russian politics
description: Explorations of how continuity and change have shaped Russian politics over the last century and what their legacies are today.

title: Discourse studies: theories and methodologies at the crossroads of language and society
description: Contemporary challenges in the broader context of discourse studies from a range of theoretical and methodological vantage points.

title: Interdisciplinarity in theory and practice
description: This collection is concerned primarily with the theory and practice of interdisciplinarity.
